title: Schema Gate: streaming mid-response schema-switch and constrained-decoder stress probe
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a targeted smoke + stress test suite that exercises schema enforcement in streaming responses when the model changes the expected schema mid-response, when tool/function calls interleave with structured output, and under constrained-decoder backoff. This ticket implements scenarios, harness plumbing, and acceptance criteria for regression prevention in runtime streaming + JSON mode combinations.
background: We regularly see partial-stream artifacts and occasional schema drift when outputs are streamed and the model switches intent or when tool calls inject fragments. Existing testbeds focus on chunk-level recovery and strict parsers, but we lack a lightweight smoke probe that asserts graceful degradation and deterministic fallbacks across model variants, quantization settings, and constrained-decoder modes.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic smoke suite (10–15 scenarios) runs in CI and flags regressions when streaming schema switches occur
Constrained-decoder backoff behavior is validated: when schema constraints cannot be satisfied within soft token budget, runtime falls back to the documented fallback policy and emits clear telemetry
Tool-call interleaving scenarios (tool returns JSON fragments + model continues streaming) do not produce unparseable final payloads more than 0.1% of runs across sampled models
A compact playbook documents manual triage steps and links to the failure dashboard for oncall and SRE
Tests cover at least three model families (small/medium/large) and two runtime modes (hosted streaming, dedicated streaming)
test_matrix: Decoder modes: constrained-decoder (strict/soft thresholds), unconstrained baseline
Interleaving: no-toolcall, synchronous-toolcall (model pauses), asynchronous-toolcall (toolcall returns mid-stream)
Failure modes: truncated stream, injected non-JSON tokens, schema version bump mid-stream, KV-cache-primed divergent prefix
test_cases: Mid-stream schema bump: start with schema v1 (flat object), after 50% tokens switch target to schema v2 (nested object). Assert parser recovers or runtime triggers fallback policy

Toolcall-fragment injection: model emits a toolcall that returns a small JSON fragment; model resumes streaming a separate JSON top-level object. Assert final combined payload is parseable or fallback is emitted

Constrained-decoder budget exhaustion: configure token soft limit; force a long structured response. Verify constrained-decoder emits sentinel + partial payload and runtime stamps telemetry with reason 'constraint-exhausted'
Truncation recovery: simulate network cut at 70% of stream. Replay with stream-resume enabled; assert that reassembled payload is either valid or clearly marked partial in telemetry
KV-cache priming divergence: prime cache with a misleading prefix then request structured output. Assert that caching does not silently change the schema shape (detect via shape fingerprinting)
test_artifacts: CI job: infra/ci/streaming-schema-smoke in GitHub Actions
notes: 2025-02-18: Kickoff — scoped to a small smoke suite to keep CI cost low; Marco and Aisha to draft runner interfaces.
2025-02-22: Decision — use existing streaming test harness; add light-weight reassembly + shape-fingerprint comparator rather than full schema validation to speed runs.
2025-02-25: Trade-off — strict full-schema validation per token is expensive; we opted for endpoint-level validation and sentinel detection in-stream plus telemetry for root cause.
2025-02-27: Review feedback from Erika (QA) — add a test that simulates toolcall latency jitter; added as test case #2.

2025-03-01: PR opened for harness and initial scenarios. CI flake observed on quantized int8 model in dedicated mode; failing 12/100 runs with partial-parse. Created ENG-214579 to investigate deterministic int8 variance.

Next steps: stabilize int8 runs, add gating thresholds to CI to avoid spurious alerts, and land the playbook for oncall triage. Plan to mark Done once CI passes on the three model families and dashboard shows <0.1% failure rate over 24h run.
